title: Infinity Policy v1
description: The rules the kernel applies. Only version and policy_id are required; the three lists default to empty. Those three lists can only RESTRICT, never grant: they can deny an effect or make it wait for a human. They cannot allow anything. The kernel itself always denies the effects deploy, authority_change and audit_delete (FORBIDDEN_EFFECT) before it reads the policy, so with every list empty and no callers map the only things that can ever be allowed are `read` and `write`. An empty policy is therefore not 'wide open': it is the least restrictive policy there is. When `callers` is present it is a per-caller grant (effects, target prefixes, risk, and action). A caller who is not listed is denied (AUTHORITY_DENIED). When `callers` is absent the kernel does not apply that check. As with proposals, the kernel is more lenient than this contract (it ignores unknown fields and denies a wrong version as UNKNOWN_POLICY_VERSION).

effects_requiring_approval.description: Effects that wait for a human (APPROVAL_REQUIRED).

risks_requiring_approval.description: Risk levels that wait for a human (APPROVAL_REQUIRED).

callers.description: Per-caller grants. When this object is present, the kernel allows a call only if caller_id is a key, the effect is listed, the target matches a prefix, and risk and action equal the grant. When this object is absent, the kernel does not apply that check. An empty object grants nobody.

target_prefixes.description: The derived target must start with one of these prefixes.
